subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should OpenClaw add a core ACP skill-context injection contract for `sessions_spawn`, and which selection modes plus prompt/observability/security semantics are allowed?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but choosing explicit/default/auto selection, redaction/audit fields, prompt layering, and Codex-native skill interaction changes a core session/security contract that automation should not decide.

options.title: Design core ACP contract first
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers specify the allowed selection modes, redaction/audit metadata, prompt layer, and Codex/native parity requirements before implementation.

options.title: Limit to existing skill filters
options.body: Do not add a per-spawn skill selector yet; rely on agent-level skill filters and existing harness-specific skill behavior until a broader prompt contract lands.

options.title: Decline core injection
options.body: Close or route future work outside core if maintainers decide ACP harnesses should not receive OpenClaw-rendered skills through `sessions_spawn`.

recommendation.title: Design core ACP contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers specify the allowed selection modes, redaction/audit metadata, prompt layer, and Codex/native parity requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the ACP thread-bound spawn surface and are the strongest history signal for the core ACP sessions contract.
